category_title: Quietly on-task students who struggle with independent inquiry and rely on peer cues
student_description: This student is quietly compliant and appears on-task, but masks significant academic struggles—particularly with reading comprehension and independent inquiry—by guessing, searching the internet, or copying peers. They rarely self-advocate or ask for help, meaning their silence often indicates confusion rather than understanding. They uniquely require proactive scaffolding, visual/read-aloud accommodations, and immediate, direct intervention the moment they signal any uncertainty.

criteria.rationale: This student struggles to independently generate scientific questions or analyze data and will silently guess if left unprompted.
criteria.check: The tutor provides explicit, step-by-step prompts or guiding questions to help the student extract information from data or text, rather than asking broad, open-ended inquiry questions.

criteria.rationale: The student relies on peer cues to start tasks and struggles with text-heavy directions.
criteria.check: The tutor uses visual aids (such as graphs or videos) or provides explicit, non-text-reliant cues to help the student initiate the task.

criteria.rationale: Because this student rarely self-advocates, any signal of uncertainty (like a thumbs-down, silence, or hesitation) must be met with immediate, direct support.
criteria.check: When the student indicates confusion, silence, or a lack of knowledge, the tutor immediately provides direct academic support or reteaching instead of telling the student to keep trying independently.
